title: Meet engineers in person: one event near you
purpose: Go to a local meetup or event in the space you want to work in, meet people, and turn each conversation into a connection you follow up on.
why: People hire people they've met. One evening at a meetup puts you in front of engineers and hiring managers who never see your applications, and a conversation about your project is easier to follow up on than a cold message. Do it once this month, then make it a habit every two weeks.
evidence: The event link, the people you met, and the follow-ups you sent.

tasks.title: Find one event near you in the space you want to work in, and register
how: Search Meetup, Eventbrite and Luma for your city plus words from your target roles: AI, agents, applied AI, your stack, or your industry (insurance, fintech, health). Founder and engineering meetups count. Online-only events don't count for this step.
tasks.done_when: You're registered for an in-person event, and its link and date are saved here.

tasks.title: Go, and meet at least three people
how: Ask each person what they're working on and what's hard about it. When they ask you, describe your project in two sentences and offer to show it.
Before you leave, connect on LinkedIn or swap an email or number with each one.
tasks.done_when: Three people's names and companies are saved here.

fields.label: Who you met: name, company, what they're working on
fields.placeholder: Dana Lee, Outmarket, building broker workflows with agents

tasks.title: Follow up within two days with one useful thing
how: Send each person a short note that names what you talked about and adds one thing: a link, an intro, or a look at your project. Add them to People on your Hire page so the follow-ups show up in your run.
tasks.done_when: Each person you met has a follow-up from you.
